artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ be a complex Hénon map, i.e., a finite composition of generalized Hénon maps $(x,y)\mapsto(p(x)-ay,x)$ with $p$ a polynomial of degree at least $2$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}^*$. Let $K^\pm$ denote the sets of points with bounded forward/backward orbits, $J^\pm=\partial K^\pm$, $J=J^+\cap J^-$, and let $\mu$ be the unique measure of maximal entropy, with support $J^*\subseteq J$. The map $f$ is said to be \emph{quasi-hyperbolic} if every periodic point in $J^*$ is a hyperbolic saddle and the stable/unstable directions extend continuously to $J^*$, yielding a continuous lamination by stable manifolds $W^s$ and unstable manifolds $W^u$ on $J^*$; equivalently, $f$ is hyperbolic on $J^*$ in the sense that the tangent bundle over $J^*$ splits continuously into uniformly contracting/expanding directions. For a point $p\in J^*$, the \emph{unstable slice} at $p$ is the connected component containing $p$ of the intersection $W^u(p)\cap K^+$ inside the unstable manifold $W^u(p)\simeq\mathbb{C}$. 

A bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ is called a \emph{John domain} if there exist a point $z_0\in\Omega$ and a constant $c>0$ such that every $z\in\Omega$ can be joined to $z_0$ by a rectifiable arc $\gamma\subset\Omega$ satisfying $\operatorname{dist}(w,\partial\Omega)\ge c\,\ell(\gamma(z,w))$ for all $w\in\gamma$, where $\ell(\gamma(z,w))$ is the length of the subarc of $\gamma$ from $z$ to $w$.

Question: If $f$ is quasi-hyperbolic, do the unstable slices of $f$ (viewed as planar domains inside the corresponding unstable manifolds) satisfy a John-type condition, in the sense that they are John domains with uniform constants?
